key_insight: Crystal-dependent recrystallization produces hourglass-like swift heavy ion tracks in rutile TiO2 but relatively uniform cylindrical tracks in anatase.
engineering_relevance: TiO2 polymorph selection can guide irradiation-based nanoscale structural modification, while accounting for recovery during characterization.
method: Compare ion-induced damage in rutile and anatase TiO2 using transmission electron microscopy.
Use molecular dynamics to investigate recrystallization during rapid cooling.
Examine electron-beam-induced changes in amorphous tracks and surface hillocks.
evidence_signal: TEM observations show contrasting track morphologies, and molecular dynamics simulations attribute these differences to polymorph-dependent recrystallization.
watch_item: Prolonged TEM electron-beam exposure can recrystallize tracks and hillocks and generate Fresnel contrast, complicating interpretation of the original irradiation damage.
paper_title: Swift Heavy Ion Tracks in Polymorphs of Titanium Dioxide: The Effects of Electron Beam and Crystal Structures
